title: Inflation and Price Levels
text: Inflation is the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises over time, corresponding to a decrease in the purchasing power of money. It is typically measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), which tracks the prices of a basket of consumer goods and services. Moderate inflation (around 2%) is considered healthy by most central banks, as it encourages spending and investment. Hyperinflation, an extremely rapid price increase, can destroy an economy's currency and savings — notable examples include Germany in 1923 and Zimbabwe in the 2000s. Central banks combat inflation primarily through raising interest rates, which reduces borrowing and spending.
